To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the surface tension of strange quark matter droplets is smaller for larger values of the electric potential at the boundary, smaller for larger values for the strangelet size and smaller for larger values (in magnitude) of the chemical potential of neutrinos.

the surface tension of strangelets decreases significantly as the boundary charge becomes more positively charged; that this occurs because the contribution of $u$ and $d$ quarks is negligible and the surface tension is dominated by the $s$ quark contribution, and that this contribution is reduced as the strangelet boundary becomes more positively charge.

(i) the surface tension of strangelets immersed in a lepto-nucleonic background is smaller when the electric charge of the strangelet is positive, and (ii) the surface tension is smaller when the temperature is higher and the chemical potential of the neutrinos is larger.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the surface properties of strangelets in different astrophysical environments.
the study of the surface tension of strangelets in compact stars.
the stability of charged strangelets and their role in astrophysics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the surface tension of strangelets in astrophysical scenarios is always smaller than that of strangelets in laboratory experiments.
the surface tension is a decreasing function of the strangelet electric charge and of the temperature.
the surface tension of charged strange matter is a very complex function of all the parameters of the problem, and that its value cannot be determined a priori.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
strangelet crusts and strangelet dwarfs with large positive electric charge at their boundaries are energetically preferred.

the presence of a lepton background and a large positive electric potential at the surface of strangelets may significantly reduce the value of the surface tension, making strangelets more likely to merge and form larger strangelets or strange stars.
the surface tension of strangelets is significantly smaller than the one obtained in previous works, and it can become even negative for the most astrophysically relevant cases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface tension of charged strange quark matter is a non-monotonic function of the electric charge at the strangelet's surface.
the surface tension of charged strange matter in the astrophysical environments considered is significantly reduced when compared to neutral strangelets.
the surface tension of strange quark matter is not a constant but a function of the strangelet size and of its electric charge.
